newsitem.title: USA: CITGO unit pays $1.23 mln for air violation.
newsitem.headline: CITGO unit pays $1.23 mln for air violation.

text.p: CITGO Asphalt Refining Co, a subsidiary of CITGO Petroleum, will pay $1.23 million in penalties for violating the Clean Air Act and will reduce sulphur oxide emissions by over 100 tons per year at a New Jersey refinery, U.S. agencies said Thursday.
CITGO Petroleum is a subsidiary of Venezuelan state oil company, Petroleos de Venezuela.

The settlement resolved allegations that the company violated Clean Air Act regulations by failing to control sulphur oxide emissions at a refinery in West Deptford, N.J., the Justice Department and Environmental Protection Agency said in a statement.
Sulphur oxides contribute to formation of acid rain, and one form of the emissions, sulphur dioxide, can irritate human lungs and worsen existing lung problems.
Beside paying the penalty, CITGO recently installed new pollution control equipment to cut sulphur oxide emissions by about 90 percent.
The EPA estimated that without appropriate controls, the refinery emitted about 140 tons of sulphur oxides per year.
